linkedin.title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered.
linkedin.body:
It felt like every time I opened a news site, I was bombarded by headlines designed only to get a click. The real stories were buried under layers of noise. I knew there had to be a better way to stay informed without feeling overwhelmed or manipulated.

Building Headlinne wasn't about reinventing the news itself. It was about changing how we interact with it. I wanted to use AI not to replace editors, but to act as a filter. The goal was simple: create a feed that learns what you care about and delivers it without the fluff.

Starting this journey young taught me that technology is only useful when it solves a human problem. You do not need more information. You need the right information, at the right time, presented in a way that respects your intelligence. We are still learning, iterating, and trying to build something that makes the daily news cycle a little less exhausting.

story_card.headline: Pope Leo leads massive Paris mass
story_card.standfirst: Hundreds of thousands gathered in Paris for the Pope's first official French visit in 18

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Pope Leo held an open-air mass for 700,000 people at the Place de la Concorde in Paris.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: This is the Pope's first official papal visit to France in nearly two decades.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The massive turnout highlights the enduring public interest in the pontiff's rare French visit.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: The Vatican will likely continue tracking the scale of public engagement throughout the trip.

story_card.caption:
Pope Leo has visited Paris for an open-air mass attended by 700000 people.

The massive crowd lined the Avenue des Champs-Élysées on the second day of the pontiff's trip. It marks a significant moment as this is the first official papal visit to France in 18 years.
